sapporo.summary: Hokkaido's capital: wide boulevards, fresh seafood, miso ramen, and an easy base for Otaru and the hot springs at Jozankei.
sapporo.best_season: February for the Snow Festival; June to August for cool, dry summers.
sapporo.getting_around: Subway lines and streetcar in the city; JR trains to Otaru and New Chitose Airport.
tips: Winter pavements are icy: bring shoes with good grip.
New Chitose Airport is about 40 minutes from Sapporo by JR rapid train.

tokyo.summary: Japan's capital mixes old temples, giant crossings, anime districts and some of the world's best food, all linked by trains.
tokyo.best_season: Late March to early April for cherry blossoms; October and November for mild weather.
tokyo.getting_around: JR Yamanote Line and the subway reach almost everything; get a Suica or PASMO IC card.
tips: Avoid trains around 8-9am on weekdays if you can: rush hour is very crowded.
Many museums close on Mondays.

morning.access: Asakusa Station (Ginza or Asakusa subway line), 5 min walk.
Tsukiji Station (Hibiya Line), 1 min walk; or Tsukiji-shijo Station (Oedo Line).

hakone.summary: Mountain hot-spring town near Mt. Fuji, known for ryokan stays, a volcanic valley and a lake cruise.
hakone.best_season: October and November for autumn leaves; clear winter mornings for Mt. Fuji views.
hakone.getting_around: The Hakone Loop (mountain train, cable car, ropeway, lake boat); the Hakone Free Pass covers most of it.
tips: Send big suitcases ahead with a luggage-forwarding service (takkyubin): the mountain train is narrow.
The ropeway can stop in strong wind or when volcanic gas levels are high.

morning.access: Chokoku-no-Mori Station (Hakone Tozan Railway), 2 min walk.
Cable car from Gora to Sounzan, then the Hakone Ropeway to Owakudani.
Moto-Hakone bus stop or boat pier, 10 min walk along the lake.

afternoon.text: Lake Ashi sightseeing cruise with Mt. Fuji views
afternoon.access: Board at Togendai (end of the ropeway) for Hakone-machi or Moto-Hakone.

mount_fuji.summary: The Fuji Five Lakes area around Kawaguchiko has the classic Mt. Fuji views, lakeside walks and onsen with the mountain in sight.
mount_fuji.best_season: October to February for the clearest views; the climbing season runs from early July to early September.
mount_fuji.getting_around: Retro sightseeing buses loop around Lake Kawaguchi and Lake Saiko from Kawaguchiko Station.
tips: Mt. Fuji hides in cloud most afternoons: plan viewpoints for early morning.
Climbing the summit trails requires booking and a fee in season; check the official trail site.

evening.text: Hoto noodle dinner
evening.access: Several hoto restaurants are within walking distance of Kawaguchiko Station.

kyoto.summary: Japan's old capital: thousands of temples and shrines, preserved streets in Gion, and traditional food.
kyoto.best_season: Early April for cherry blossoms; mid-November to early December for autumn leaves.
kyoto.getting_around: City buses and the subway; walk between Gion, Kiyomizu-dera and Higashiyama.
tips: Visit Fushimi Inari and Arashiyama before 8am to avoid crowds.
Photographing geiko and maiko on private Gion streets is banned; respect the signs.

nara.summary: Japan's first permanent capital, with a giant bronze Buddha and deer roaming freely in a huge park.
nara.best_season: Spring and autumn; Nara is an easy day trip from Kyoto or Osaka.
nara.getting_around: Most sights are a walk from Kintetsu Nara Station.
tips: Deer crackers (shika senbei) are sold in the park; deer can nip, so hold them up and away.
Kintetsu Nara Station is closer to the park than JR Nara Station.

osaka.summary: Japan's kitchen: street food, neon-lit Dotonbori, a famous castle and Universal Studios Japan.
osaka.best_season: All year; spring and autumn are the most comfortable.
osaka.getting_around: The Midosuji subway line links Umeda, Namba and Tennoji; Kansai Airport is 40-70 minutes away.
tips: Book Universal Studios Japan tickets and Express Passes in advance.
Stand on the right on escalators in Osaka (the left in Tokyo).

hiroshima.summary: A city of peace and remembrance, and the gateway to Miyajima Island's floating torii gate.
hiroshima.best_season: Spring and autumn; check Miyajima's tide times to see the torii at high tide.
hiroshima.getting_around: Streetcars in the city; JR train plus ferry to Miyajima (about 1 hour).
tips: Allow at least two hours for the Peace Memorial Museum.
Miyajima has a small visitor tax collected with the ferry fare.

fukuoka.summary: A relaxed seaside city famous for tonkotsu ramen and open-air yatai food stalls, with the airport minutes from downtown.
fukuoka.best_season: Spring and autumn; summer festivals in July.
fukuoka.getting_around: Subway from the airport to Hakata (5 minutes) and Tenjin; buses for the waterfront.
tips: Yatai stalls open around 6pm and close in bad weather.
Dazaifu is about 40 minutes away by Nishitetsu train.

okinawa.summary: Subtropical islands with beaches, coral reefs, Ryukyu Kingdom history and its own food culture.
okinawa.best_season: April to June and October; July to September is hot with typhoon risk.
okinawa.getting_around: Yui Rail monorail in Naha; a rental car is the easiest way to reach the beaches and the north.
tips: Driving needs an International Driving Permit (or a Japanese licence).
Shuri Castle's main hall is being rebuilt after a 2019 fire; the grounds are open.

niseko.summary: Hokkaido's best-known ski area: deep, dry powder snow under the cone of Mt. Yotei, with an international resort village.
niseko.best_season: Mid-December to March for powder snow (best in January and February); summer for hiking and rafting.
niseko.getting_around: Free or cheap shuttle buses link Grand Hirafu, Hanazono, Niseko Village and Annupuri in winter; Kutchan is the nearest JR station.
tips: Book accommodation, ski lessons and rental gear months ahead for the Christmas, New Year and Lunar New Year peaks.
The Niseko United all-mountain pass covers the four linked resorts.
Respect closed gates and avalanche warnings: off-piste is only allowed through the official gates.

hakuba.summary: A valley of ski resorts below the Northern Japan Alps, host of the 1998 Winter Olympics, with onsen and mountain views.
hakuba.best_season: December to early April for skiing; January and February for the snow monkeys nearby. Summer and autumn for hiking.
hakuba.getting_around: Free shuttle buses connect the main resorts and villages in winter; taxis are limited, so book ahead in the evening.
tips: The Hakuba Valley pass covers lifts at the main resorts across the valley.
Send ski bags ahead with a luggage-forwarding service (takkyubin) rather than carrying them on trains.
Restaurants in Echoland and Happo fill up early in peak season: reserve dinner.
